criteria.quote: "Zubat is blind, but its colonies may sound different."
criteria.revision: Open with: "Zubat has no eyes—but the frequency of its ultrasonic waves can differ from colony to colony." This makes the unusual contrast more precise and immediately grounded in the research.

criteria.quote: "frequencies can differ slightly between colonies" and "It emits waves from its mouth, then reads their reflections."
"If Zubat navigates by sound, why can colonies use slightly different frequencies?"
criteria.revision: Change the open loop to: "If Zubat’s ultrasonic waves check its surroundings, what exactly differs from colony to colony—the sonar’s job, or only its frequency?" The supplied research can clearly answer that the frequency differs slightly, while the navigation function remains the same.

criteria.quote: "It has no eyes, so ultrasonic waves check obstacles in darkness." → "It emits waves from its mouth, then reads their reflections." → "frequencies can differ slightly between colonies."
criteria.revision: Make the sequence build toward the reveal: establish that Zubat is eyeless, specify that the waves come from its mouth and are read through reflections, then reveal the colony-level frequency difference. Move "The variation is slight" into the payoff instead of using it as a separate near-restatement.

criteria.quote: "Zubat is blind, but its colonies may sound different."
criteria.revision: Do not reveal the colony variation in the first scene. Open with: "Zubat has no eyes, yet it flies through darkness by emitting ultrasonic waves from its mouth." Save "the frequency of those waves can differ slightly from colony to colony" for the fourth scene, making the variation the actual turn.

criteria.quote: "SOUND REPLACES SIGHT" / "ZUBAT READS REFLECTIONS" and "FREQUENCIES CAN DIFFER" / "DIFFERENT DOESN'T MEAN OPPOSITE"
criteria.revision: Replace the fifth scene’s restatement with a distinct colony detail supported by the research: "Zubat colonies also gather in caves and old buildings during the day—and when it gets cold, they gather to warm one another." Keep the frequency reveal separate from the colony behavior.

criteria.quote: "Zubat shares eyeless ultrasonic sonar across colonies, while its frequencies can differ slightly from group to group."
criteria.revision: Use a sharper resolution: "The surprising part isn’t that Zubat uses ultrasonic sonar—that stays consistent. It’s that the frequency can still differ slightly from colony to colony." This resolves the opening contrast without claiming the research explains why the frequencies differ.

criteria.quote: "Which is cooler: eyeless sonar or colony variation?"
criteria.revision: Make the split more evidence-specific: "Which is the bigger surprise: that Zubat has no eyes, or that its ultrasonic frequency can differ slightly from colony to colony?"
